caption:
What happens if something changes after you fly home?
Usually nothing. The part that is not nothing tends to arrive late.

Three windows. The first week is swelling and bruising, expected and settling. The first month is when the result arrives, and most disappointment with it. The months after are when rare, late reactions can appear - and you will already be home.

In a retrospective review of 4,500 patients treated with one hyaluronic acid filler, 44 delayed reactions were recorded: just under 1% per patient, appearing a median of four months after treatment, and all of them resolved. One product, two clinics, charts rather than a trial. It is not a rate for every filler or every treatment. It does say that late is a real timeline.

So set three things up before you board. The exact product, amount and date, in writing rather than memory. Who you contact, and how, from another time zone. And one clinician at home who has seen that record.

Sudden pain, blanching or a change in vision is same-day emergency care, wherever in the world you are.

General education only.

#FillerComplications #DelayedReaction #MedicalTourism #MedicalAesthetics #KoreanAesthetics
first_comment: Aftercare is not a leaflet. It is a phone number that answers. What did you actually get to take home with you?
